activation.details: Wrapper script re-applies the patch per hotspot bring-up; no reboot or service restart needed.

payload.effects: The AP serves 160 MHz on channels 36 and wider, giving HE160-capable clients their maximum link width; already-connected clients experience a short AP flap (about 0.5-2 s) during the Disconnect/SelectNetwork cycle; the width is runtime-only and must be re-applied on every bring-up.
payload.explanation: A wrapper script runs the whole sequence per bring-up: regdom country change with a verified retry loop, nmcli device set managed yes, nmcli connection up of the 36/80 base profile, then the wpa_supplicant D-Bus patch (GetInterface s <iface> on the object root, CurrentNetwork read for the network path, set-property of the four fields, Disconnect, SelectNetwork) and an iw dev width poll. Nothing persistent is changed: the NetworkManager profile itself stays at base 80 MHz, the width lives only in wpa_supplicant runtime state, and the procedure must be re-run every time the hotspot is raised. A companion off-script restores the original regulatory country. Regulatory responsibility: the chosen country code must be lawful in the country of use.

steps: Set the global regulatory country to one allowing 160 MHz at 5150-5350 MHz (this machine uses ID: sudo iw reg set ID) and confirm the global line of iw reg get before raising the access point
Raise the base profile: sudo nmcli connection up <AP-160-profile> ifname <iface> (it comes up on channel 36 at 80 MHz)

Find the runtime objects: sudo busctl --system call fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1 /fi/w1/wpa_supplicant1 fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1 GetInterface s <iface> gives the interface path; sudo busctl --system get-property on that path with fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1.Interface CurrentNetwork gives the network object path

Patch the network: sudo busctl --system set-property fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1 <network-path> fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1.Network Properties a{sv} 4 frequency i 5180 ht40 i 1 max_oper_chwidth i 2 vht_center_freq1 i 5250
Re-associate: sudo busctl --system call on the interface path Disconnect, sleep 0.5, then SelectNetwork o <network-path>

Poll sudo iw dev <iface> info until it shows width: 160 MHz (about 2 s). If it never does, fall back with nmcli connection down/up for a working 36/80 AP, and restore the original regulatory country when the hotspot is turned off

payload.rollback: Nothing persistent to undo: restore the regulatory country (sudo iw reg set <original>) and cycle or leave the profile down; the base profile is unmodified.
payload.validation_plan: After the patch, iw dev <iface> info reports width: 160 MHz within a few seconds and HE160-capable clients connect to the hotspot; deliberately skipping the patch leaves the same AP functioning at 36/80 as the fallback path.
